doc.title: Etta Jones interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 2, 1998

title: Theater shows at the Apollo
summary: Six shows a day, with movies and newsreels, for about 35 cents.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: In the theaters that you played in those days, was that the situation in those days, where they would show movies, and you would play a few times during the day?

Yeah. Sometimes we would be on call as soon as we got off the stage because there would be six shows a day at the Apollo sometimes. They’d say, “Half an hour is in” so that meant you had half an hour before you started all over again, to get yourself together.
And could the audience stay there all day?
How much did it cost to get it? Do you recall?
And two movies and a show, and a chapter and the news, everything.
